text:
marta: uploaded preliminary bring-up for draft-model-12b-4bit. Highlights: ~1.8x tokens/s vs fp16 on p4d, median E2E latency improvement ~12ms when speculative prefetch is on. full artifacts: gs://redwood-experiments/draft-onboard/7987659999/

hussein: cool. was that using the two-stage speculative path or plain prefetch?

marta: two-stage (fast candidate generator + fallback sampler). config attached below. noted a small regression on the abstractive summarization holdout.

oliver: small meaning what magnitude?

marta: ROUGE-L dropped ~0.6 absolute, human likert median -0.2. Perplexity stayed about the same, so it's likely a ranking/style shift rather than model calibration.

sara: paste the decode/quant config so we can repro.

marta: ```
speculative: {
  enabled: true,
  fast_sampler: {type: "top-k", k: 40, temp: 0.9},
  fallback_sampler: {type: "top-p", p: 0.95, temp: 1.0},
  fast_token_budget: 6
}
quant: {bits: 4, scheme: "q8_0_like", per_channel: true}
runtime: {batching: auto, kv_cache: prefix_warm:true, max_seq: 2048}
```

aaron: did you try with KV warm-prefix off? speculative prefill can interact with prefix caching in weird ways.

marta: yes 3 with warm-prefix on we see +7-9% token/s, but ROUGE hit remains. Turning warm-prefix off reduces throughput but the ROUGE difference disappears.

hussein: that suggests stale/incorrect KV entries from prefetch affecting early token ranking. any concrete examples in the logs?

marta: uploaded a few transcripts. Example: short news-summary prompt with ambiguous lead-in. Fast sampler produced a short stylistic continuation that drifts from the reference; fallback would have steered it back but we commit early due to the early-commit heuristic.

oliver: our early-commit threshold is p>0.7, right? If fast outputs have locally high prob but globally worse, we should tighten that or increase fast_token_budget. Worth testing.

sara: propose A/B matrix: 1) baseline fp16 no speculative; 2) quant (4-bit) no speculative; 3) quant + speculative (current); 4) quant + speculative with commit p>0.85 and warm-prefix off. Keep batch/seq equal.

marta: I'll queue those. We'll run 2k summarization holdout + 2k dialog-longform holdout. Capture ROUGE/ROUGE-L/CLIPScore + 200 human likert judgements per arm for largest deltas.

aaron: for human eval do blind pairwise with anchors and randomize order. Also capture TTF token; product cares more about time-to-first-token than median E2E sometimes.

hussein: add an "exposure_ratio" metric: fraction of tokens produced by fast sampler vs fallback. That should correlate throughput gain with any quality change.

marta: good idea. logging fast_tokens/total_tokens per request.

ci-bot: build 7987659999-spec-onboard started (matrix: p4d, quant=4bit, runtime=speculative). ETA ~45m.

oliver: another lightweight trick: force greedy for first 2 tokens in fast sampler then switch to top-k. Early tokens tend to anchor style.

sara: also add a recency-sensitive factuality holdout (QA F1). Speculative prefetch could hallucinate older context into the early tokens.

marta: will run arms x seeds(3) x holdouts(2). adding an arm 5: cheap embedding-based rerank on first 8 tokens to prefer fallback when similarity low.

hussein: reranker idea is promising since it's cheap and parallelizable. If it works we can keep throughput benefits but cut regressions.

sara: timeline? product expects a recommendation for Dedicated customers by EOW.

marta: automated CI done ~50m from now, automated metrics in ~2h, human eval within 48h. I'll post interim when automated completes.

hussein: please tag me on the final note and include a short ops checklist for Dedicated rollout (limit knobs, runtime flags, safe presets). We should keep speculative as opt-in with docs on tradeoffs.

marta: will do. tagging @hussein. thanks all :thumbsup:
